title: Leaving a module out, which the review sheet offers as the way past a Will refuse limit, ends with Submit refused as "unknown module CP-MODEL" and no run starts.
expected: CT-022 and CT-030: the review sheet's 'Leave out <module>' button (and the Advanced 'Requested modules' list) let the analyst run a pathway without a module; once approved, Submit starts the run. src/deploy_workflow/inbox/scheduler.py:323 and web/src/pages/connected/api.ts:384 must agree on whether CP-MODEL may be in a module list.
actual: After 'Leave out Legal & covenants' the sheet showed 'Modules (13)' and 'Left out: Legal & covenants'; approval and the 'Start a synthetic test?' dialog worked; confirming returned to /start step 3 with the alert 'unknown module CP-MODEL Review the run again before submitting.' and no run (HTTP 400). Unticking one module under Advanced > Requested modules fails the same way. The server refuses any code not in cpos_launch.METHODS (scheduler.py:323; CP-MODEL is not in it, checked), while api.ts:384 says CP-MODEL 'is sent, never drawn as a module'. The button also moves the analyst back to More context without saying so. The code is in the shared scheduler, so the regular mode is likely affected; not run (R4).
suggested_change: Make the two agree (the server accepts CP-MODEL in a module list, or the client drops it before Submit and the server re-adds it); show the reason in analyst words if a list is ever refused; add a test that submits a list with one module left out.

title: An analyst who accepts the review sheet's Will refuse limit gets a Failed run with the reason "stopped: checker", four of 14 modules finished and no report, not the five limited modules the sheet described.
expected: The review sheet (Limits to decide) says Legal & covenants 'stops' and 'Also affects' four named modules, and the analyst accepts 'these 5 limits'; CT-040: a blocked module still delivers a Bottom line saying why, downstream modules stop at their own gate, nothing is skipped; CT-030: an accepted limit lets the run proceed.
actual: Following docs/react-workflow.md (filing and workbook only), accepting all four limits, approving and confirming gave: Failed, 'stopped: checker', 4 of 14 modules finished, Legal & covenants 'Interrupted', nine modules and the Report 'Not run', three 'Module draft rejected' events, no Open report link. Nine modules the sheet never named as affected did not run. The only reason shown is two internal words. Probably a property of the canned synthetic handoffs (the checker rejects the Legal & covenants draft), so stage 4 decides whether it is proof-only; the analyst cannot tell. The documented route's missing agreement upload is carried from stage 0 and not registered again here.
suggested_change: Either deliver a blocked Legal & covenants handoff in the synthetic proof so an accepted limit is demonstrable, or state on the sheet that the synthetic test cannot run without the agreement; show the refusal reason ('No executed governing document') in the run's failure line instead of 'stopped: checker'.

screen: /start step 4, any pathway but Full credit assessment (error)
title: The synthetic test lets the analyst choose, review, approve and submit seven of eight pathways, every one of which ends Failed with "launcher exited 2; see logs/<run>.log".
expected: CT-012 to CT-019: each offered pathway can be run; a failure says what went wrong in words the analyst can act on. Product Principle 2: a limit is a decision the analyst makes, not a line they scroll past.
actual: Lite (5 modules), Deep (20), Earnings Update, Relative Value, Covenant & Refinancing, Distressed & Restructuring and Portfolio Decision were each reviewed, approved and confirmed ('spends USD 0.00'); each run page read 'Failed ... launcher exited 2; see logs/<id>.log' and 0 modules finished. The reason sits in a file the analyst cannot open: 'synthetic proof requires a first Credit Snapshot run' (proof/launcher.py:100). Neither the Purpose step, the review sheet nor the dialog says only Full runs in the synthetic test. The message also shows a server-side path. All seven were submitted in the journey record (Earnings Update only after supplying the two periods it requires, see J1-004); the probe tries Lite and Deep.
suggested_change: State on the Purpose step and the review sheet that the synthetic test runs only the Full credit assessment (do not remove the cards, R5), and put the launcher's own sentence in the run's failure line instead of an exit code and a log path.

title: For Earnings Update, Current period and Prior period are required, but the step says "Optional", neither field is marked, and the only signal is the browser's own tooltip.
expected: CT-007 and the step text: 'Optional. You can continue if the documents provide all the context.' A required field is marked, and the page reports it in its own error style, as it does for other fields (for example 'Observed quotes · Quote 1 · Provider: required.').
actual: With Earnings Update chosen, pressing Review run with both fields empty stayed on step 3: the browser showed 'Please fill out this field.' on Current period; no in-page alert, no error summary, no 'required' on the labels. After filling Current period the same happened on Prior period. The faded placeholders 'q3-2026' and 'q2-2026' read like filled values. A quote row with a missing Provider, by contrast, produced an in-page alert.
suggested_change: Mark Current period and Prior period as required when the pathway needs them, change the step intro for that pathway, and report the missing field with the page's own alert.

title: Your name is required but unmarked; the first complaint comes at Review run, which returns the analyst to step 1 and resets the stepper to Not started.
expected: CT-009: analyst name is required; docs/react-workflow.md 'Open the interface' lists the steps to run the proof. A required field is marked where it is asked.
actual: Following the documented steps (which never mention a name), Review run on step 3 jumped back to Documents with 'Enter your name as your first name and initial, for example Eric G'. The stepper then showed steps 2 to 4 'Not started' although the answers were kept (purpose, agreement and workbook were still set when the analyst went forward again). The analyst clicks through three steps again.
suggested_change: Mark Your name as required on step 1, validate it on Continue, and keep completed steps shown as complete after a return.

title: The review sheet calls the workbook 'unrecognised' under Documents read yet a Check on the same sheet recognises it as a portfolio workbook, and the Portfolio workbook row says 'Among the documents' instead of naming the chosen file.
expected: CT-008: the sheet states which file is the portfolio workbook and the page reads each file and lists what it found. One screen gives one status per file.
actual: 'northbridge-portfolio.xlsx · unrecognised' appears under Documents read; when the workbook was not chosen the Check for Committee decision says 'A portfolio workbook or the fund's portfolio export is among the documents ... Found: northbridge-portfolio.xlsx'. When it was chosen, the Context row reads 'Among the documents' (and 'Not given' when it was not), never the file name. The sample filing is also 'unrecognised', which raises two acknowledgements ('Whole run' and 'Financial foundation') about a file the instructions told the analyst to upload.
suggested_change: Show one status per file, name the chosen workbook in the Portfolio workbook row, and give the sample files a recognised kind or a note that they are test files.

title: A Check tells the analyst to 'choose it as the portfolio workbook under Issuer and dates', but no section has that name; the field is on the More context step.
expected: CT-007 and CT-008: the fix text points to where the control is. The page has 'Issuer and case date' (step 1) and 'More context' (step 3).
actual: The Check (src/deploy_workflow/run_expectations.py:664) names 'Issuer and dates'; the sheet shows no such heading and offers no button to the right step for this Check, although the README says a Check with a fix has a stage to go to.
suggested_change: Say 'under Portfolio workbook on the More context step' and add a go-to-step button.

screen: /runs (full, with one failed and one finished run)
title: Run activity counts and lists only runs that ended without a report; the finished run appears nowhere on it and the 'Ended' tile reads 1 after two runs ended.
expected: CT-035 and apps/issuer-library/README.md ('Run activity'): the page lists runs as queued, running, finished, failed and so on.
actual: After one Failed run and one Finished run, Run activity showed Running 0, Waiting 0, Ended 1 and a table titled 'Ended without a report' with only the failed run. The hint 'Finished runs are in the library' appears only on the empty page.
suggested_change: Label the tile 'Ended without a report' and show the library pointer whenever the page is shown.

title: The same 14 modules appear in three orders (run page, Modules navigator and Evidence filter, Overview), and the Overview's 'Bottom line by module' lists 13 while the navigation says Modules 14.
expected: CT-023 and CT-044: one module order and one count across screens; Committee decision should be findable where the others are.
actual: Run page: Research questions fourth, Legal & covenants fifth, Committee decision last. Modules navigator and Evidence filter: Research questions last, Legal & covenants eleventh. Overview 'Bottom line by module' omits Committee decision, whose line is the report's lead Bottom line (trace drawer: 'Committee decision · Handoff line 28'), so the list has 13 rows beside a badge of 14.
suggested_change: Use the run order everywhere and add Committee decision to the per-module list or say the lead line comes from it.

title: Four different screens carry the same page title 'Credit OS', so browser tabs, history and screen readers cannot tell them apart.
expected: PRODUCT.md Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA working assumption), success criterion 2.4.2: each page has a descriptive title. The report pages already do ('Overview — <issuer> — Credit OS').
actual: document.title is 'Credit OS' on the library, Start a run, Run activity and a run's progress page; only report tabs change it.
suggested_change: Set the title per route, for example 'Start a run — Credit OS' and '<issuer> run — Credit OS'.

title: The left rail holds two icon-only links with no visible text or tooltip; the play-circle icon reads as 'start' but opens Run activity.
expected: Design: a first-time analyst can tell where each control leads. The page's own 'Start a run' button is the real start.
actual: The rail links have an accessible name ('Library', 'Run') but no title, no text and no tooltip after a 1.2 s hover. The play-circle link goes to /runs, not /start.
suggested_change: Show a label beside or under each icon, or a tooltip; name the second link 'Run activity'.

title: 'Run activity' names two different screens (the list at /runs and one run's progress page at /run/<id>), and the rail calls the list 'Run'.
expected: One name per screen. The progress page's own breadcrumb ('Run activity / Northbridge Synthetic Group') uses it for the list.
actual: The report's 'Run activity' button opens /run/<id> (one run); the progress page's breadcrumb 'Run activity' opens /runs (the list); the rail link is named 'Run'.
suggested_change: Name the report button 'Run progress' or 'This run's activity' and the rail link 'Run activity'.

title: The same case date and run times are written in four formats across the run page, report, library card and Run activity.
expected: One date format across screens (display of a period or date never changes spelling).
actual: As-of: '2025-03-31' (run page, library card) and '31 March 2025' (report header). Times: 'Finished at 07:46:16 UTC' (run page) and '17 Nov 2026, 07:46 UTC' (Run activity).
suggested_change: Pick one date format and one time format for all screens.

title: The documented synthetic steps name buttons that do not exist ('Review inputs', 'Approve summary') and omit the required analyst name; stage 0 already carried the missing agreement upload.
expected: docs/react-workflow.md:108-117 is 'the synthetic run, step by step' and should match the screen.
actual: The screen offers 'Continue to purpose', 'Continue to context', 'Review run', a checkbox 'Approve: I have read this summary and want this run started' and 'Submit run'. There is no 'Review inputs' or 'Approve summary'. Following the text exactly, the analyst meets the name error (J1-005) and the Will refuse limit (J1-002); the document names neither.
suggested_change: Rewrite the paragraph with the real button names, the name, the agreement upload and its selection under Legal documents.

title: 'Start from this run' opens with today's date in As-of date and an empty Your name, although the page says to 'add dates' and the README says the analyst's own name is kept; the documents list says 'No documents yet' until Inspect documents is pressed.
expected: apps/issuer-library/README.md:208: not carried are the as-of date, periods and the submitter 'the analyst's own name is kept'; the page text 'Review the copied answers, add dates, and inspect its available documents.'
actual: From the Failed run, As-of date read 2026-11-17 (the default for any new page, not the run's 2025-03-31) and Your name was empty after the analyst had typed 'Ana L' moments before. The Documents list read 'No documents yet.' although the run's documents were available; Inspect documents listed them. The portfolio workbook choice was not carried and the sheet then raised a Check for it (documented, but not said at the step).
suggested_change: Leave As-of date empty (or carry it as a marked suggestion) in this mode, keep the name, and list the carried documents on arrival.

title: The word 'Purpose' names three things: the step (the pathway), the 'Run purpose' select (market view) and the review row 'Purpose', while 'Edit purpose and modules' edits the pathway.
expected: One meaning per label (CT-012 to CT-019 name the pathway; the select is the market-view purpose).
actual: Step 2 'Purpose' holds the eight pathway cards and a 'Run purpose' select (No market view / New issue / Trading). The review sheet lists 'Pathway: Full credit assessment' and 'Purpose: No market view (research)'.
suggested_change: Rename the step 'Pathway' (or the select 'Market view').

title: Two lines on the review sheet cannot be understood by the analyst: 'Fixed below the Advanced form level.' and, under a full 14-module list, 'Report sections omitted · What changed since the last Report'.
expected: PRODUCT.md Principle 1: the analyst commits knowing what the run will and will not do; wording names a thing the analyst can act on.
actual: With nothing left out the sheet still says 'Report sections omitted · What changed since the last Report' below Modules (14), which reads as if sections were dropped; 'Fixed below the Advanced form level.' sits under Model and effort without saying what is fixed or why.
suggested_change: Say 'Changes: not compared (first run of this pathway)' in that place and 'Model and effort are set at the Advanced form level' for the other.

title: The README says the run's cap is shown 'beside each pathway and before Submit'; the pathway cards show no cap and the cap appears only in the Readiness card for the chosen pathway.
expected: apps/issuer-library/README.md:162 and CT-021: the cap is shown on the Purpose step beside each pathway (Lite 15, Full 25, Deep 40, purpose pathways 20).
actual: The eight cards show a name, one sentence and 'N base modules'. The Readiness card reads 'USD 0.00 of USD 25.00' and changed to 15 and 40 when Lite and Deep were picked. The paid confirmation ('Start a paid run?') is not reachable under proof.serve, so what it says about the cap was not seen.
suggested_change: Show each pathway's cap on its card, or correct the README to say the cap follows the choice in Readiness.

title: proof.serve refuses any root that already holds a file, so a restarted synthetic service cannot reopen earlier runs; the refusal is argparse usage text.
expected: docs/react-workflow.md 'Open the interface' (use a new folder for the manual proof) and the lead's stage 3 note that run state persists in the root so a later segment can reopen it.
actual: Starting proof.serve on /tmp/jr/j1, which held a finished and a failed run, exited 2 with 'the synthetic proof requires an empty, separate run root' (proof/serve.py:19-20). The synthetic proof therefore cannot show a reload after a service restart, a resumed or interrupted run, or a second run that follows a restart; each journey segment must run inside one service session.
suggested_change: none: a fragile assumption for the audit and the work-PC proof; the owner may decide whether the proof should allow reopening a root.
